subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation guard explicit hostname allowlists permit non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the SSRF hardening from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100835?
rationale: The source conflict is clear, but the correct outcome depends on maintainer intent for an SSRF trust boundary that protects against DNS rebinding while also enforcing a browser-owner allowlist contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow browser exception
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101991 or equivalent code that restores only the explicit browser allowlist case while keeping metadata, link-local, and unintended rebinding blocked.

options.title: Retire the old allowlist contract
options.body: Keep the stricter SSRF rule and update the browser navigation guard test/docs so non-localhost names resolving to loopback are not accepted without explicit localhost/loopback or private-network opt-in.

options.title: Split the trust model first
options.body: Hold the fix until browser navigation policy and shared SSRF resolver policy have separate owner-approved contracts for operator-declared endpoints.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow browser exception
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101991 or equivalent code that restores only the explicit browser allowlist case while keeping metadata, link-local, and unintended rebinding blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent maintainer-side history on both the merged SSRF hardening and adjacent browser CDP policy fixes.
